claims.source_quote_ar: انتصابه على أنه حال مؤكدة منه
claims.claim_ar: وضع كلمة «قَائِمًا بِالْقِسْطِ» منصوبًا كحال مؤكدة لتأكيد صفة القيام بالعدل.
claims.claim_en: The phrase «قَائِمًا بِالْقِسْطِ» is deployed as a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl) — an emphatic ḥāl — to stress the attribute of standing in justice.
claims.needs_review_reason: Mapping the syntactic note about an emphatic ḥāl to the provided maani subtypes is somewhat interpretive; the best-fit subtype chosen is 'fasl_wasl' although the source describes 'انتصاب حال' rather than explicitly using the listed subtype names.

claims.claim_ar: الآية تستعمل سجلّ الشهادة (اللَّهُ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ وَأُولُو الْعِلْمِ) كأسلوب احتجاجي لتأكيد التوحيد.
claims.claim_en: The verse uses testimonial witnesses (God, the angels, and those of knowledge) as a method of argumentation — invoking testimony as rhetorical proof for tawhīd (divine oneness).

claims.claim_ar: تكرار صيغة التوكيد «لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ»/نحوها يعمل كوسيلة بلاغية للتوكيد على وحدانية الله.
claims.claim_en: The formula 'there is no god but He' (or the very similar construct quoted) functions as a rhetorical repetition used to emphasize God's uniqueness.
claims.needs_review_reason: The quoted substring comes from the commentary's discussion of the formula '(إِلهٍ إِلَّا اللَّهُ)' in a related context; tying it specifically to the double occurrence in the ayah is plausible but the source chunk does not explicitly analyze the ayah's repetition using the technical term 'تكرار'.
